content.title: Steph Curry impressive in return, but Rockets edge Warriors
content.text: April 5, 2026Updated April 6, 2026, 1:18 a.m. ETStephen Curry's return was not enough to lift the Golden State Warriors past the Houston Rockets in a 117-116 loss on Sunday night. Curry made his return to the court after missing the past two months due to an injury.The Warriors haven't been at full strength for seemingly the entire season. But with five games left to go before the postseason begins, the team was able to get Curry back on the court.Curry's was questionable for the game, but the NBA's all-time leading three-point shooter made his return to the Warriors on Sunday night's game. Curry had missed 27 consecutive games due to a persistent knee injury.The Warriors had posted a 9-18 record in those 27 games without Curry. Golden State is locked into the Play-In Tournament, but Curry's return could bring some much needed momentum to a team that has suffered season-ending injuries to Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody. Rockets vs. Warriors highlights Stephen Curry plays a key role in returnStephen Curry finished the game with 29 points and four assists in 26 minutes of play in the Warriors' loss to the Rockets on Sunday. He shot 11-of-21 from the field and was 5-of-10 from the 3-point line. Stephen Curry scores 10 points in first half for WarriorsStephen Curry shot 4-for-10 from the field for 10 points in 11 minutes of play in the first half. Curry was also 2-for-5 from the 3-point line and did not reach the free-throw line. He also had one rebound and an assist. Stephen Curry in first quarter vs. RocketsHe finished the quarter with three points and an assist in five minutes of play against the Rockets. He was 1-for-4 from the field and 1-for-3 from the 3-point line. The Warriors lead the Rockets 31-26. Stephen Curry comes off benchCurry was not named in the starting lineup and will come off the bench with 4:54 left in the first quarter. Stephen Curry prepares for return Steph Curry arrives for Warriors' game vs. Rockets How many games did Stephen Curry play this season?Stephen Curry played in 39 games in what has been an underwhelming season for the Golden State Warriors. The Warriors have a 36-41 overall record and are currently the 10th seed. Stephen Curry is expected to play tonightGolden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr told reporters that Curry is expected to play against the Rockets on Sunday. The two-time MVP, who has not played since Jan. 30, is expected to play around 25 minutes, according to coach Steve Kerr, playing in "small bursts." How to watch Stephen Curry's returnStephen Curry will make his return as the Golden State Warriors host the Houston Rockets at the Chase Center in San Francisco on Sunday night.When: Sunday, April 5, 2026Where: Chase Center (San Francisco)TV: NBCStream: PeacockStream Warriors vs. Rockets on PeacockIs Steph Curry playing tonight vs. the Houston Rockets?It hasn't been officially announced yet as of 3:15 p.m. PT, but all indications are that Curry will be cleared to play Sunday night for the first time in over two months. ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater first reported on Curry's impending return on Friday, April 3.Official word from the Warriors on Curry's status will likely come closer to Sunday night's 7 p.m. local time tip-off.Steph Curry statsPrior to injuring his knee in February, Curry was averaging 27.2 points, 3.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 39 games played this season, while shooting 46.8% from the field, 39.1% on 3-pointers and 93.1% on free throws.Curry participated in a scrimmage at Warriors practice on Friday, and head coach Steve Kerr came away from it hopeful about his star."Everything went well. Yeah, he looked good," Kerr told reporters. "He’s pretty good. He looks like Steph Curry."Warriors playoff outlookGolden State has been in turmoil ever since Curry went down. They were already dealing with several injuries, but being without their best player sent them spiraling. The Warriors went 9-18 in the 27 games Curry missed, but his return is just in time for the most important time of the year.Though they won't be able to catch the sixth seed, the Warriors' spot in the play-in tournament is set. With five games left to go in the regular season, Golden State currently holds the 10th and final seed as they trail the seventh-seeded Phoenix Suns by six games and the No. 9 Los Angeles Clippers by three."Yeah, I mean he brings hope to a tough situation," Kerr told reporters on Friday. "I thought [Spurs] game, we were never really in the game, but the guys fought, they competed, they stayed with it until the end. The vibe was good. When Steph’s around, the vibe tends to be better. It’s definitely better right now so hopefully we’ll have another good effort tonight and he’ll be on the sidelines cheering. We’ll see how it goes the next couple of days but we’re obviously dying to get him back.”
